objective: Standard statement: (1) correction of ticket A, Theorem 5: its proof reduced exactness of a nonnegative not-all-equal law to non-2-colourability of G plus the corner triple, but the right reduction is non-2-colourability of G with the three corners merged, and its claim overlooked the one-triangle gadget (exact for every law); prove the corrected statement that no nonnegative not-all-equal law is exact on a gadget with 2 <= n <= 6 triangles, using m(3) = 7 when the corner triangles are distinct and a forcing lemma (no 2-colourable 3-graph with at most five edges forces two vertices equal) when two corners share a triangle; (2) duality at the knot angle: on a gadget whose contacts are all three-fold with an odd number of base incidences (then exactly one each), the signed knot's mixed sector sums are (-i sqrt3)^(n-1) times signs times not-all-equal colouring counts of the dual configuration (triangles as points, contacts as lines), so the knot is exact iff the dual is 2-colourable and the dual plus the corner triangle line is not; (3) hence such gadgets need at least 7 triangles, and with distinct corner triangles the 7-triangle ones are exactly the Fano gadgets (Fano plane, corner triangles on one line); (4) the 64 Fano gadgets are linear, exact for the signed knot and for plain not-all-equal (so the corrected bound is sharp), and not generic. Nearest known result: property B (m(3) = 7, the Fano plane); ticket A. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved by SPACE-SELECTION-20261030-001C-P001 (V1): corrects ticket A's Theorem 5 (wrong hypergraph in the proof, n = 1 overlooked): no nonnegative not-all-equal law is exact for 2 <= n <= 6, sharp at 7; at the knot angle a gluing whose contacts are three-fold with odd base count is plain not-all-equal on its dual configuration, so the knot needs at least 7 triangles there and, with distinct corner triangles, exactly the 64 Fano gadgets, which are exact for both the signed and the plain knot.
title: Three-fold contacts: the knot on phases, the Fano gadget, and the corrected interference bound
